<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **151** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 935d80a3d4b6e337314997b83aee55fd651d2106 && git checkout 935d80a3d4b6e337314997b83aee55fd651d2106
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1 9cb2180be17e97f065d85cd64c7816b031cd2344 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1 && git merge --no-ff 9cb2180be17e97f065d85cd64c7816b031cd2344

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9cb2180be17e97f065d85cd64c7816b031cd2344`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts + packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/rest/src/import-upsert-in-file-duplicate-key.test.ts (the narrowing floor: every path outside the prose faces), and the cited code: packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts (coerceRow, coerceFieldValue, CoerceContext, isBlank, matchOption, the reference branch), packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts (the sync import door and the async import-job worker, both runImport callers), packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts (runImport caller), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts (runImport caller), packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.test.ts (the ledger's own pins), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (the disposition categories), scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs (the face read off the file list). The prose faces read for the claim they make: .changeset/26133-import-duplicate-match-key.md, content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx, content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx, contract.mdx, error-code-ledger.mdx, export.mdx. Read-only at the head via git show refs/seat/pr26250 and git diff against c7aa9cde24ca7d17563caa4e01037f3ab1b9e990; the dispatch order and the seat's own conclusions were not inputs.

Face note: the brief asked for the narrowing face; `record-recognisers --paths` over the PR's file list reads the schema face off packages/spec/src/api/*.zod.ts (a published schema is in the committed tree). Both map to the one tier named above, so the record stands on either reading; the Scope line carries the schema hits first and the narrowing floor after them.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. Narrowing: an `update` or `upsert` import whose rows repeat one coerced match key now answers every such row `ok: false`, `action: 'failed'`, `code: 'DUPLICATE_MATCH_KEY'` and writes none of them; `insert` is untouched (`rowsSharingKey` returns an empty map before any work). RIGHT, and it is the triage ruling 6417860878 verbatim: detect in-file duplicate keys before any write, refuse those rows with a row-level error naming the row numbers. The message names every row of the key and the key set.

2. The pre-pass coerces only the key columns, through the SAME `coerceRow` and the SAME `coerceCtx` object the row's own pass now uses (the context literal was lifted out of the loop, not copied). Read against import-coerce: `coerceRow` iterates `Object.entries(rawRow)` and `coerceFieldValue` is per-cell with no cross-field dependency, so a key cell coerces identically whether or not its non-key siblings are present. Trim and `nullValues` go through `isBlank`, option labels and values through `matchOption`, lookups through the shared `resolveRef`, dates and numbers through the same parsers; `keySetOf` is the one helper `findExisting` now shares, so the set a row is grouped by is the set the matcher queries by. RIGHT.

3. Coercing twice has no second side effect. `createMissingOptions` keeps the raw value and REPORTS it as `keptOptionValues`; the option is only admitted on the write that carries that context, and the pre-pass discards its kept list, so nothing is created twice. `resolveRef` caches only definitive hits (id or ambiguous) and never a miss, so the pre-pass warms the cache the row's pass reads; the self-object flush branch is dead during the pre-pass because `pendingCreates` is empty. The pre-pass swallows a thrown coercion and a cell error alike by dropping the key (the row's own pass reports them), so no row gains a second error channel. RIGHT.

4. Key equality by `JSON.stringify([keySets.indexOf(keySet), values])`: coerced numbers are numbers ("1" and 1 agree), options are the option value, lookups are the target id string, dates are the parser's one output per cell so two equal cells serialise alike, multi-value cells are arrays compared in order exactly as the matcher's `where` would pass them. The index of the key set is in the key, so a row matched by set 0 and a row matched by set 1 never collide, which is what the matcher does (it queries one set only). `keySetOf` requires every member non-blank, so no `undefined` reaches the serialiser. RIGHT; the exact-compare boundary under a case-insensitive MySQL collation is named in the PR's acceptance notes and is the matcher's own boundary, not a new one.

5. Dry run: the `shared` check sits before the `dryRun` branch in the row loop, so the preview and the write answer the same rows from the same code path; the unique-index object's preview, which used to say created, created while the write said created plus UNIQUE_VIOLATION, now agrees on both halves. RIGHT, and pinned by the test file (dry results equal real results minus ids).

6. Every runImport caller gets the one behaviour: the sync door and the async job in data-action-routes spread `prepared` into the same call; the connector pull (upsert on `upsertKey`) and the user import (`email` / `phone_number`, `skipBlankMatchKey: true`) run the same runner. `ImportRowResult.code` is an open `string`, so no caller's type narrows; the UI wording fallthrough is noted below. RIGHT.

7. Progress and yield accounting: the pre-pass yields to the event loop every `progressEvery` rows, so a synchronous driver cannot starve the cancel route during it; it reports no `onProgress` snapshot (nothing is processed yet) and `processed`, `total`, `errors` in the row loop are unchanged, so an async job's counters are still truthful. A refused row counts in `errCount` exactly as an `AMBIGUOUS_MATCH` row does. `shouldCancel` is not polled during the pre-pass, so a cancel lands at the first checkpoint of the row loop instead; a delay, never a lost cancel. RIGHT, non-blocking.

8. The spec: `DUPLICATE_MATCH_KEY` joins `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/core']` beside `AMBIGUOUS_MATCH` and `BLANK_MATCH_KEY`, the runner being its first reader (D5); the `matchFields` description in export.zod.ts says what it means; the four references under content/docs/references/api are the `gen:docs` projection (the `+344 more` to `+345 more` deltas and the one enum row each). No sharded artifact carries the ledger's members (grep of api-surface, json-schema.manifest and authorable-surface for AMBIGUOUS_MATCH finds none), so the regenerated set is complete. RIGHT.

One boundary the claim text does not name (non-blocking, no local run): a key column that is a lookup to THIS object, pointing at a row the same file creates earlier, resolves `reference_not_found` in the pre-pass (nothing is buffered yet) and so has no key there; in the row loop the self-object flush resolves it. Two such rows sharing a key therefore still answer created then updated at this head. It is the pre-existing in-file self-reference corner, not a regression, and outside the card's repro; it belongs in the PR's acceptance notes or a follow-up card, not in this landing.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-26T17:02Z: success on Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Lint ESLint, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint docs and code guards, Lint scoped (tooling self-tests, slot lookup and corpus, query-options erasure), Lint PM dispatch-gates, Type Check source gates, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, Flag docs, Check Documentation Links, the card-claims-branch, part-of and single-writer guards, Auto Label, filter. Still pending at that read: Lint and Repo Gates (queued aggregate), Test Core 1 through 8, Build Core, Type Check workspace, Type Check debt ledger, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check UI, Build and E2E UI. Skipped by path filter: Dogfood Verify CLI and shards, Temporal Conformance, Lint UI, Test UI, the opt-in tarball and 18.x harness. Nothing red. The queue lands only on every required context green, so the pending set is the queue's to wait for, not this record's to pre-judge.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/26133-import-duplicate-match-key.md`: `@objectstack/core: patch`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`. The diff moves core (the runner) and spec (one ledger member plus contract text), and no other published package. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: an error code is not a key, value or type a metadata author writes, and `ImportRequestSchema` accepts exactly what it accepted. The rule for `none` is patch, and a non-protocol narrowing ships patch while keeping its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition; both are present. `Clause-②: no (narrowing: ...)` is line-initial in the PR body and the changeset, the one closed arm, spelled identically in both. The BREAKING paragraph states the before and after and the caller's move (keep one row per key, import again). The ADR-0087 marker is exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; its body prescribes no consumer rewrite (there is no FROM to TO, no tombstone, no key change), so the category's own refusal does not bite, and Check Changeset is green on this head. The new ledger member is a widening of the closed `ApiErrorSchema.code` union, published from spec; that is the ordinary D5 registration of a code with a reader and takes no changeset level beyond patch. Level: RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag: `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx` (one row in the hand-written per-row outcome table) outside the claim's listed surface. IN BOUNDS: the claim's prohibition reads `No other packages/spec/** edit`, which this path is not; the table lists every per-row code and would otherwise advertise a vocabulary narrower than the runtime delivers. The tree's `meta.json` needs no change (no page added).
- Dev flag: the four `content/docs/references/api/*.mdx` files `gen:docs` regenerated. IN BOUNDS and mandatory: AGENTS.md's spec-artifact rule makes a `.describe()` change regenerate `gen:schema && gen:docs` before push, and `check:docs` would red without them; `Type Check source gates` is green on this head.
- `open_questions: []` in the dev report: nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (noted, not filed): the case-insensitive MySQL collation pair is unmeasured and reads as the matcher's own exact-compare boundary; the Console's `ImportWizard` wording falls through to the server's English error, which names the rows. Both are acceptance notes, not reproducible defects; noting is the right disposition under Prime Directive 10.
- The unique-index widening: the dev attributes refusing duplicates on unique-index objects too to a seat ruling in the server seat 2 thread at 2026-10-26T14:56Z. That ruling is not among the card's three comments (triage, claim, dev report); the card itself carries only the triage ruling 6417860878, which already says detect before any write and refuse those rows, with no object-class exception, so the behaviour stands on the card's own ruling. ESCALATED as a record hygiene point: a ruling the dev cites should be on the card for the next reader; no change to the diff.
- Face: the committed tree touches two published schema files, so the schema face also applies; same tier, no second record owed.
- The in-file self-reference corner named under ① is the one open boundary; recommended as an acceptance note or a follow-up card, not a blocker.
